patch_description: Warm-start the Gauss-Seidel radius solver inside the shift search: cache the previous radii vector and use it as initialization for the next candidate evaluation. Since each shift moves only one circle slightly, radii converge in a handful of sweeps instead of needing full cold 300-sweep solves. This cuts the ~9s runtime dramatically, and the freed budget funds more refine–shift fixed-point outer rounds (3→6), which historically each squeeze out a bit more sum (~2.49 → higher).
